verdict_convention: Judge pre-inversion yes/no. Negated EF/AQ items record whether the named flaw is present, not the post-inversion score.

identifies_the_mechanism.rationale: Root cause is a traffic spike, not the pool-versus-worker mismatch.

grounded_in_evidence.rationale: Points at metrics.csv request counts and the 14:02 deploy as a failed throughput fix.

rules_out_the_decoy.rationale: Vendor advisory is called unrelated because latency stayed flat.

separates_contributing_factors.rationale: Load-shed, planning, and autoscaling gaps are distinct from the spike claim.

uncertainty_is_genuine.rationale: Asks which campaign drove the spike; no marketing ticket is supplied.

fixes_the_capacity_coupling.rationale: Autoscaling and load-shed do not couple pool size to workers.

closes_the_detection_gap.rationale: No pool-saturation or acquire-wait alert is added.

actions_are_actionable.rationale: Autoscale, load-shed 503, capacity ticket, and standby region are concrete.

actions_trace_to_findings.rationale: Actions follow the document's spike and admission-control findings.

proposes_unsupported_work.rationale: Treats a traffic-spike capacity program as remediation for this incident.

asserts_unsupported_cause.rationale: An unforecasted traffic spike is asserted as the cause.

misstates_a_fact.rationale: Reads ~1200 req/5min as a surge even though that is the pre-incident baseline in metrics.csv.

invents_evidence.rationale: Uses metrics.csv; no invented dashboards or people.
